topic.name: Lower Riemann Sums Over General Rectangular Partitions

question.text:
Let $R = [3,4] \times [5,6]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 4x^2+7y^2-12.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where \begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

Given that the lower Riemann sum of $f$ with respect to $P$ is given by \[ L(f,P) = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n \fbox{$\phantom{AAAAA}$} \: \Delta x_i \Delta y_j \] where $\Delta x_i = x_{i} - x_{i-1}$ and $\Delta y_j = y_{j} - y_{j-1},$ what is the missing expression in the double summation above?
question.explanation:
The lower Riemann sum is given by \begin{align*} L(f,P) &= \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n m_{ij}\Delta x_i \Delta y_j \end{align*} where $m_{ij}$ is the minimum value of $f$ in each subregion $R_{ij}.$

We consider an arbitrary subregion $R_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$ over the $x$-axis and $y_{i-1}$ and $y_i$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • $f(x,y) = 4x^2 + 7y^2 - 12$ increases as $x$ increases on $[3,4],$ and

  • $f(x,y) = 4x^2 + 7y^2 - 12$ increases as $y$ increases on $[5,6].$

As a result, the minimum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the smallest possible $x$ and the smallest possible $y.$ This is the value at the bottom left corner of each subregion.

Therefore,

\begin{align*} m_{ij} &= f(x_{i-1}, y_{j-1}) = 4x_{i-1}^2 + 7y_{j-1}^2 - 12 \end{align*} for all $1\leq i\leq m$ and $1\leq j\leq n.$

Finally, the lower Riemann sum is \begin{align*} L(f,P) & = \sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n ({\color{blue}{4x_{i-1}^2 + 7y_{j-1}^2 - 12}})\Delta x_i \Delta y_j. \end{align*}

So, the missing expression is $4x_{i-1}^2 + 7y_{j-1}^2 - 12.$

question.text:
Let $R = [3,5] \times [2,7]$ be a region in the $xy$-plane, and let $f(x,y) = 40 - x - 4y.$ Further, let $P$ be a partition of $R,$ where

\begin{align*} P_1 = \left\{x_0,x_1,\ldots, x_m\right\}, \qquad P_2 = \left\{y_0,y_1,\ldots, y_n\right\}, \qquad P = P_1\times P_2. \end{align*}

We consider an arbitrary subregion $R_{ij}$ of the partition. This subregion lies between $x_{i-1}$ and $x_i$ over the $x$-axis and $y_{i-1}$ and $y_i$ over the $y$-axis, as shown below.

Notice that:

  • $f(x,y) = 40 - x - 4y$ decreases as $x$ increases, and

  • $f(x,y) = 40 - x - 4y$ decreases as $y$ increases.

As a result, the minimum value of $f$ in each subregion is attained when we have the largest possible $x$ and the largest possible $y.$ This is the value at the top right corner of each subregion.

Therefore, \begin{align*} m_{ij} & = f(x_{i}, y_{j}) = 40 - x_{i} - 4y_{j} \end{align*} for all $1\leq i\leq m$ and $1\leq j\leq n.$

So, the missing expression is $40 - x_{i} - 4y_{j}.$
